text:
sam-support: Customer reported function call args arriving as partial/malformed JSON when using streaming response. They see tool invocation land in our logs with args truncated mid-object.

sam-support: Example from their server log: `request_id=rc-9a3b4c`
```
EVENT: toolcall.start id=rc-9a3b4c model=gptx-streaming
PAYLOAD: {
  \"tool\": \"search\",
  \"args\": {
    \"query\": \"Top 5 error causes for latency in the last 24h, filter by \"
}
```

sam-support: The payload above ends abruptly (see escaped quote). They only see the trailing `}` for the toolcall metadata but args body is cut. Customer reproduces reliably when streaming tokens; non-streaming calls are fine.

jin-ml: Hmm — this looks like the stream was cut while the model was still emitting the JSON. Two immediate suspects: (1) proxy or client closing the connection early due to max buffer/timeouts, (2) our streaming chunker/truncation logic hitting an internal threshold.

maria-devex: Can you ask for the raw chunk stream? If they can run `curl -N` and capture the raw bytes we can see whether chunks include the complete JSON broken across chunks or whether the final chunk is missing.

sam-support: Asked customer for curl capture and they attached two snippets: one from their edge (nginx) and one from our backend. Edge shows last chunk received is `... \"query\": \"Top 5 error causes for la` and then the connection closed. Backend shows we wrote the full tokens out.

leo-infra: This points at an intermediary truncating. Do they have `proxy_buffering on` or timeouts like `proxy_read_timeout 60s`? Also check `proxy_http_version` — for streaming we require `1.1` with `chunked_transfer_encoding` allowed. Some old load balancers mishandle chunked streams.

sam-support: Customer says they have an older F5 appliance and an nginx sidecar. F5 is a likely culprit. They also said enabling `http2` on the edge made it worse.

jin-ml: Repro steps we should ask them to run (minimal):
1) Reproduce with `curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream\"` and pipe to a file.
2) `tcpdump -w stream.pcap host api.redwood.example and port 443` while reproducing.
3) Provide request_id header we return and the exact time window.

maria-devex: Also ask them to try streaming to a raw `nc` server to ensure their client library isn't the problem (some Node libraries buffer until EOF). Example Node repro: 
```js
fetch(url, {headers, method: 'POST'})
  .then(r => {
    const reader = r.body.getReader();
    // read chunks and console.log with indexes
  });
```
If the client buffers, chunks will appear intact locally but the edge may split differently.

sam-support: Suggested immediate workaround: (a) switch to non-streaming tool call for now, (b) send `args` base64 encoded in the prompt/metadata (so it's not parsed by streaming JSON decoder), (c) upgrade/disable the F5 chunk coalescing or set the nginx `proxy_buffering off` on their side. Customer tried `proxy_buffering off` on nginx and saw improvement but still saw rare truncations.

leo-infra: We should add server-side mitigations: 1) make our streaming emitter append an explicit end-of-toolcall sentinel token (e.g., `\n<TOOLCALL_END>\n`) after JSON so downstream can detect incomplete messages; 2) log per-chunk sequence ids in the backend so we can compare what we sent vs what the last chunk the edge reported.

jin-ml: Agree on sentinel — low-risk and backwards-compatible. Also add an opt-in header `X-Redwood-Stream-Sentinel: true` for a quick rollout to affected customers only. Ops: can we ship a flag?

ops-bot: rollout_request: owners=eng-runtime,priority=high,impact=customers_reporting_truncation

maria-devex: Action items: 
- sam-support: collect pcap + raw curl output + request_id from customer (owner: sam)
- leo-infra: test common LB configs (nginx+f5) against a local streaming endpoint to reproduce and document recommended config (owner: leo)
- jin-ml: prototype sentinel and per-chunk sequence logging (owner: jin)

sam-support: I'll ping the customer for pcap and confirmed request_id=rc-9a3b4c and window 2026-03-14T21:13:00Z-21:14:00Z. I'll also advise non-streaming short-term workaround.

leo-infra: For the internal playbook I'll try reproducing with both `proxy_buffering on` and `off`, and with `proxy_http_version 1.0` vs `1.1`. Preliminary notes: old F5 versions (<v14) seem to close a chunked stream early if health checks/idle timers kick in.

jin-ml: For observability: correlate backend `toolcall.start` token emission logs with `toolcall.complete` and emit metrics for "incomplete_tool_calls" when we see start without a matching completed JSON parse. That will help quantify impact.

sam-support: Customer is satisfied with the mitigation path if we add sentinel and produce recommended LB configs. Moving to escalations queue and will update ticket #SUP-11287.

maria-devex: Good. If anyone gets a pcap/hex dump, drop it here and I'll assist with parsing the chunk boundaries. :mag:

sam-support: will follow up once I have the pcap. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
